units.zh: 列傳第五十 明四王
units.en: Biographies 50: the four sons of Emperor Ming who received princely rank.
units.literal: Biography 50: The Four Princes of Ming.

units.zh: 明帝十二子：陳貴妃生後廢帝，謝脩儀生皇子法良，陳昭華生順帝，徐婕妤生第四皇子，鄭脩容生皇子智井，次晉熙王燮，與皇子法良同生。
units.en: Emperor Ming fathered twelve sons: Consort Chen’s son became the later deposed ruler; Lady Xie’s son was Prince Fa-liang; Lady Chen the Bright Consort bore Shun; Lady Xu the Fourth Prince; Lady Zheng bore Prince Zhijing; next came Prince Xie of Jinxi, Fa-liang’s full brother.
units.literal: Emperor Ming had twelve sons: Honored Consort Chen bore the later deposed emperor; Lady Xie Xiuyi bore Prince Fa-liang; Lady Chen Zhaohua bore Emperor Shun; Lady Xu Jieyu bore the Fourth Prince; Lady Zheng Xiurong bore Prince Zhijing; next Prince Xie of Jinxi, born of the same mother as Prince Fa-liang.

units.zh: 泉美人生邵陵殤王友；
units.en: Lady Quan gave birth to Prince You, posthumously ennobled as Prince Shao-ling.
units.literal: Lady Quan the Meiren bore Prince You, posthumously titled Prince Shao-ling;

units.zh: 次江夏王躋，與第四皇子同生。
units.en: Next was Prince Ji of Jiangxia, the Fourth Prince’s full brother.
units.literal: Next Prince Ji of Jiangxia, born of the same mother as the Fourth Prince.

units.zh: 徐良人生武陵王贊，杜脩華生隨陽王翽。
units.en: Lady Xu of lower rank bore Prince Zan of Wuling; Lady Du the Accomplished bore Prince Hui of Suiyang.
units.literal: Lady Xu the Liangren bore Prince Zan of Wuling; Lady Du Xiuhua bore Prince Hui of Suiyang.

units.zh: 次新興王嵩，與武陵王贊同生。
units.en: Then came Prince Song of Xinxing, Prince Zan’s full brother by the same mother.
units.literal: Next Prince Song of Xinxing, born of the same mother as Prince Zan of Wuling.

units.zh: 又泉美人生始建王禧。
units.en: Lady Quan also bore Prince Xi of Shijian.
units.literal: Again Lady Quan the Meiren bore Prince Xi of Shijian.

units.zh: 智井、燮、躋、贊並出繼。
units.en: Zhijing, Xie, Ji, and Zan were each given in adoption to continue collateral houses.
units.literal: Zhi-jing, Xie, Ji, and Zan all went out to continue other lines.

units.zh: 法良未封，第四皇子未有名，早夭。
units.en: Fa-liang died before investiture; the Fourth Prince never even received a personal name—both perished in childhood.
units.literal: Fa-liang received no fief; the Fourth Prince never received a name; both died young.

units.zh: 邵陵殤王友字仲賢，明帝第七子也。
units.en: Prince You of Shao-ling, styled Zhongxian, was the seventh son of Emperor Ming.
units.literal: Prince You of Shao-ling, courtesy name Zhongxian, was Emperor Ming's seventh son.

units.zh: 後廢帝元徽二年，太尉、江州刺史桂陽王休範反誅，皇室寡弱，友年五歲，出為使持節、督江州豫州之西陽新蔡晉熙三郡諸軍事、南中郎將、江州刺史，封邵陵王，食邑二千戶。
units.en: In 474, after Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled and was executed while serving as Grand Commandant and governor of Jiang Province, the royal house was enfeebled. At five years old, You was sent out as Prince of Shao-ling and governor of Jiang Province, bearing the credentials of authority and command over the three Jiang–Yu commanderies of Xiyang, Xincai, and Jinxi, with a fief of two thousand households.
units.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui of the Later Deposed Emperor, when Grand Commandant and Governor of Jiang Province Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled and was executed, the imperial house was weak; You, aged five, went out as bearer of the credentials of authority, Director of military affairs of the three commanderies Xiyang, Xincai, and Jinxi in Jiang and Yu provinces, General of the South Center, Governor of Jiang Province, enfeoffed Prince of Shao-ling, with revenue from two thousand households.

units.zh: 府州文案及臣吏不諱有無之有。
units.en: In princely and prefectural archives and among his clerks and attendants, they did not observe the taboo against the word you in the phrase "having or not having" (because it matched You's name).
units.literal: In princely and prefectural documents and among clerks and officers, they did not taboo the you in you wu (having or not having).

units.zh: 順帝即位，進號左將軍，改督為都督。
units.en: When Shun came to the throne, You was promoted to General of the Left and his title of director was upgraded to commander.
units.literal: When Emperor Shun ascended the throne, he was promoted to General of the Left, and Director was changed to Commander.

units.zh: 昇明二年，徙都督南豫豫司三州諸軍事、安南將軍、南豫州刺史、歷陽太守。
units.en: In 478 he was transferred to commander over South Yu, Yu, and Si provinces, made General for Pacifying the South, governor of South Yu, and administrator of Liyang.
units.literal: In the second year of Shengming, he was transferred to Commander over military affairs of South Yu, Yu, and Si provinces, General for Pacifying the South, Governor of South Yu Province, and Administrator of Liyang.

units.zh: 三年，薨，無子，國除。
units.en: He died in the third year (479); heirless, his fief was abolished.
units.literal: In the third year, he died; with no son, the state was abolished.

units.zh: 隨陽王翽字仲儀，明帝第十子也。
units.en: Prince Hui of Suiyang, styled Zhongyi, was the tenth son of Emperor Ming.
units.literal: Prince Hui of Suiyang, courtesy name Zhongyi, was Emperor Ming's tenth son.

units.zh: 元徽四年，年六歲，封南陽王，食邑二千戶。
units.en: In 476, at the age of six, he was made Prince of Nanyang with a fief of two thousand households.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui, aged six, he was enfeoffed Prince of Nanyang, with revenue from two thousand households.

units.zh: 昇明元年，為使持節、督郢州司州之義陽諸軍事、西中郎將、郢州刺史。
units.en: In 477 he was appointed bearer of the credentials of authority, director of Yiyang military affairs in E and Si provinces, General of the West Center, and governor of E Province.
units.literal: In the first year of Shengming, he was made bearer of the credentials of authority, Director of military affairs of Yiyang in E and Si provinces, General of the West Center, and Governor of E Province.

units.zh: 未拜，徙督湘州諸軍事、南中郎將、湘州刺史，持節如故。
units.en: Before taking up that post, he was transferred to governor of Xiang Province as General of the South Center, retaining his credential-bearing commission.
units.literal: Before he received the appointment, he was transferred to Director of military affairs of Xiang Province, General of the South Center, and Governor of Xiang Province, still holding the credentials of authority.

units.zh: 未之鎮，進號前將軍。
units.en: Before he took up his post, he was promoted to General of the Front.
units.literal: Before he went to his command, he was advanced to General of the Front.

units.zh: 二年，以南陽荒遠，改封隨陽王，以本號停京師。
units.en: In 478, because Nanyang was too remote, his fief was moved to Suiyang and he was kept at the capital under his existing rank.
units.literal: In the second year, because Nanyang was remote and desolate, he was re-enfeoffed Prince of Suiyang and remained at the capital with his former rank.

units.zh: 齊受禪，降封舞陰縣公，食邑千五百戶。
units.en: When the Qi founder took the throne, Hui was reduced to county duke of Wuyin with fifteen hundred households.
units.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was demoted to Duke of Wuyin County, with revenue from one thousand five hundred households.

units.zh: 謀反，賜死。
units.en: Convicted of plotting rebellion, he was ordered to take his own life.
units.literal: He plotted rebellion and was granted death.

units.zh: 新興王嵩，字仲嶽，明帝第十一子。
units.en: Prince Song of Xinxing, styled Zhongyue, was the eleventh son of Emperor Ming.
units.literal: Prince Song of Xinxing, courtesy name Zhongyue, was Emperor Ming’s eleventh son.

units.zh: 元徽四年，年六歲，封新興王，食邑二千戶。
units.en: In 476, at the age of six, he was made Prince of Xinxing with a fief of two thousand households.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui, age six, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xinxing, with revenue from two thousand households.

units.zh: 齊受禪，降封定襄縣公，食邑千五百戶。
units.en: When the Qi founder took the throne from the Song, Prince Song was reduced to county duke of Dingxiang with fifteen hundred households.
units.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was demoted to Duke of Dingxiang County, with revenue from one thousand five hundred households.

units.zh: 謀反，賜死。
units.en: Convicted of plotting rebellion, he was ordered to take his own life.
units.literal: He plotted rebellion and was granted death.

units.zh: 始建王禧，字仲安，明帝第十二子也。
units.en: Prince Xi of Shijian, styled Zhongan, was the twelfth son of Emperor Ming.
units.literal: Prince Xi of Shijian, courtesy name Zhongan, was Emperor Ming’s twelfth son.

units.zh: 元徽四年，年六歲，封始建王，食邑二千戶。
units.en: In 476, at the age of six, he was made Prince of Shijian with a fief of two thousand households.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui, age six, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shijian, with revenue from two thousand households.

units.zh: 齊受禪，降封荔封縣公，食邑千五百戶。
units.en: When Qi succeeded the Song, Xi was demoted to county duke of Lifeng with fifteen hundred households.
units.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was demoted to Duke of Lifeng County, with revenue from one thousand five hundred households.

units.zh: 謀反，賜死。
units.en: Convicted of plotting rebellion, he was ordered to take his own life.
units.literal: He plotted rebellion and was granted death.

units.zh: 史臣曰：太宗負螟之慶，事非己出，枝葉不茂，豈能庇其本根。
units.en: The historians observed that Mingdi’s line rested on an adopted succession: those sons were not truly of his own issue, and a sparse canopy of twigs cannot shield the trunk.
units.literal: The historians say: Taizong bore the blessing of the adopted heir; the matter was not born of himself; branches and leaves were not lush, and so could not shelter the root.

units.zh: 侯服於周，斯為幸矣。
units.en: To end merely as a Zhou-style fief-holder was, under the circumstances, the kinder fate.
units.literal: To be enfeoffed as a lord under the Zhou—this was fortune enough.

units.zh: 順皇帝諱準，字仲謀，[1]小字智觀，明帝第三子也。
units.en: Emperor Shun, taboo name Zhun, courtesy name Zhongmou, [1] childhood name Zhiguan, was the third son of Emperor Ming.
units.literal: Emperor Shun, taboo name Zhun, courtesy name Zhongmou, [1] childhood name Zhiguan, was the third son of Emperor Ming.

units.zh: 泰始五年七月癸丑生。
units.en: He was born on the guichou day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Taishi.
units.literal: He was born on the guichou day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Taishi.

units.zh: 戊辰，崇拜帝所生陳昭華為皇太妃。
units.en: On the wuchen day the emperor's birth mother, Consort Chen of the Zhaohua rank, was honored as Grand Imperial Consort.
units.literal: On the wuchen day the emperor's birth mother, Lady Chen, who held the consort rank Zhaohua, was honored as Grand Imperial Consort.

units.zh: 七年，封安成王，食邑三千戶。
units.en: In the seventh year he was created Prince of Ancheng with a fief of three thousand households.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ancheng with a fief of three thousand households.

units.zh: 仍拜撫軍將軍，置佐史。
units.en: He was at once appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, with aides and clerks assigned.
units.literal: He was at once appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, with aides and clerks established.

units.zh: 廢帝即位，為揚州刺史。
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor acceded, he became Inspector of Yangzhou.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor acceded, he became Inspector of Yangzhou.

units.zh: 元徽二年，進號車騎將軍、都督揚南豫二州諸軍事，給鼓吹一部，刺史如故。
units.en: In the second year of Yuanhui he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Yang and South Yu provinces, granted one set of martial pipes and drums, and remained Inspector as before.
units.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui he was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the two provinces of Yang and South Yu, granted one set of martial pipes and drums, and remained Inspector as before.

units.zh: 四年，又進號驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，班劍三十人，都督、刺史如故。
units.en: In the fourth year he was further promoted to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, authorized to maintain his own office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and granted thirty ceremonial swordsmen; he remained Commander-in-Chief and Inspector as before.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was further advanced to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, granted authority to establish his own office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and thirty ceremonial swordsmen, and remained Commander-in-Chief and Inspector as before.

units.zh: 元徽五年七月戊子夜，廢帝殞，奉迎王入居朝堂。
units.en: On the night of the wuzi day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Yuanhui, the Deposed Emperor died; the prince was escorted into the court hall.
units.literal: On the night of the wuzi day of the seventh month of the fifth year of Yuanhui, the Deposed Emperor died; the king was welcomed and entered to dwell in the court hall.

units.zh: 壬辰，即皇帝位。
units.en: On the renchen day he ascended the throne.
units.literal: On the renchen day he assumed the imperial throne.

units.zh: 昇明元年，改元，大赦天下，賜文武位二等。
units.en: In the first year of Shengming the era name was changed, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and civil and military officials were advanced two ranks in status.
units.literal: In the first year of Shengming the era name was changed, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm, and civil and military officials were granted two ranks in status.

units.zh: 丙申，詔曰：「露臺息構，義光漢德；
units.en: On the bingshen day an edict said: "Ceasing construction on the Terrace of Dew shed light on Han virtue;
units.literal: On the bingshen day an edict said: "Ceasing construction on the Terrace of Dew shed light on Han virtue;

units.zh: 九月己丑，詔曰：「昔聖王既沒，淳風已衰，龜書永湮，龍圖長祕。
units.en: On the jichou day of the ninth month an edict said: "When the sage kings passed away, pure custom had already decayed; the Tortoise Book lay forever hidden and the Dragon Chart long sealed away.
units.literal: On the jichou day of the ninth month an edict said: "When the sage kings passed away, pure custom already declined; the Tortoise Book was forever submerged and the Dragon Chart long concealed.

units.zh: 桂陽王休範在鎮，數出行遊，韜性方峙，未嘗隨從。
units.en: While the Prince of Guiyang, Xiufan, was in command he went out on pleasure tours again and again; Tao, upright and unyielding by nature, never went along.
units.literal: When the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan, held the post, he often went out touring; Tao's nature was upright and stern, and he never followed along.

units.zh: 泰始末，爲征南江州長史。
units.en: At the close of Taishi he served as chief aide to the Pacify-the-South General for Jiangzhou.
units.literal: At the end of Taishi he was chief aide on the Pacify-the-South staff for Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 丙午，以安西參軍明慶符為青、冀二州刺史，武陵王贊為郢州刺史，新除郢州刺史南陽王翽為湘州刺史，司空、南兗州刺史齊王改領南徐州刺史，征虜將軍李安民為南兗州刺史。
units.en: On the bingwu day Ming Qingfu, staff officer of Anxi, was appointed Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces; Prince of Wuling Zan was appointed Inspector of Yingzhou; Prince of Nanyang Hui, newly appointed Inspector of Yingzhou, was appointed Inspector of Xiangzhou; the Prince of Qi, Minister of Works and Inspector of South Yanzhou, was reassigned to hold concurrently Inspector of South Xuzhou; Li Anmin, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was appointed Inspector of South Yanzhou.
units.literal: On the bingwu day the Anxi staff officer Ming Qingfu was made Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces; the Prince of Wuling Zan was made Inspector of Yingzhou; the newly appointed Inspector of Yingzhou, Prince of Nanyang Hui, was made Inspector of Xiangzhou; the Prince of Qi, Minister of Works and Inspector of South Yanzhou, was changed to hold concurrently the post of Inspector of South Xuzhou; Li Anmin, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.

units.zh: 庚午，司空長史謝朏、衞軍長史江斅、中書侍郎褚炫、武陵王文學劉候入直殿省，參侍文義。
units.en: On the gengwu day Xie Fei, chief clerk to the Minister of Works; Jiang Xiao, chief clerk of the Guards Army; Chu Xuan, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat; and Liu Yu (the received text has Liu Hou), Literary Scholar to the Prince of Wuling, entered duty in the palace offices to advise on literary matters.
units.literal: On the gengwu day Xie Fei, chief clerk to the Minister of Works; Jiang Xiao, chief clerk of the Guards Army; Chu Xuan, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat; and Liu Yu (the received text has Liu Hou), Literary Scholar to the Prince of Wuling, entered duty in the palace offices to assist with literary matters.

units.zh: 征西大將軍、荊州刺史沈攸之進號車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，尚書左僕射、中領軍、鎮軍將軍、南兗州刺史齊王為司空、錄尚書事、驃騎大將軍，刺史如故，中書令、衞將軍、開府儀同三司，撫軍將軍劉秉為尚書令，加中軍將軍，[2]安西將軍、郢州刺史晉熙王燮為撫軍將軍、揚州刺史，南陽王翽為郢州刺史。
units.en: Shen Youzhi, General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and authorized to maintain his own office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies. The Prince of Qi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Central Army Commander, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of South Yanzhou, was appointed Minister of Works, Recording Secretary, and Grand General of Agile Cavalry, remaining Inspector as before. [2] The text is defective here; the collation note restores the missing appointments: Yuan Can became Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister over the Masses, while Chu Yuan became Guards General, and both were authorized to maintain their own offices with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies. Liu Bing, General Who Pacifies the Army, became Director of the Masters of Writing and additionally Central Army Commander. Xie, Prince of Jinxi, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, became General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yangzhou. Prince of Nanyang Hui became Inspector of Yingzhou.
units.literal: Shen Youzhi, General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry and granted authority to establish an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies. The Prince of Qi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Central Army Commander, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of South Yanzhou, was made Minister of Works, Recording Secretary, and Grand General of Agile Cavalry, remaining Inspector as before. [2] The text is defective here; the collation note restores that Yuan Can was made Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister over the Masses, while Chu Yuan was made Guards General, and both received authority to establish offices with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies. Liu Bing, General Who Pacifies the Army, was made Director of the Masters of Writing and additionally Central Army Commander. Xie, Prince of Jinxi, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yangzhou. Prince of Nanyang Hui was made Inspector of Yingzhou.
